beside this file (ROADMAP 5.4). Each of the six checklist items
points at the object it is a claim about, derived from the frozen
statement and bound to its hash.

statement_matches_text.why_not: Whether the Lean statement says what the natural-language text says is a comparison between a formal object and a sentence in English. No property of the formal object settles it: con-leche accepts A06_wrong_statement, and con-leche is a checker with a model-theoretic consistency proof. The material below is what the reviewer must read side by side; the verdict is theirs and is recorded nowhere else.

material_to_read.claim_text: Every Fermat number 2^(2^n) + 1 is prime (Fermat, c. 1640).

in_the_statement.note: `^` is RIGHT-associative: `2 ^ 2 ^ n` is `2 ^ (2 ^ n)`, not `(2 ^ 2) ^ n`. A Fermat number is the former; the two agree only at n = 1.
The class instance behind `^`; which `Monoid` it resolves through decides what the base and exponent types are.
Mathlib's `Nat.Prime` is irreducibility in ℕ: 0 and 1 are NOT prime and 2 is the smallest. A text defining a prime as 'divisible only by 1 and itself' admits 1 and does not match this.
A numeral's type is inferred, so `2` in a statement may not be the Nat the text means.
The instance that makes a bare numeral a Nat; its absence where a numeral appears means the numeral is something else.

no_unintended_convention.limit: An empty `in_the_statement` means no constant on that list appears, NOT that the statement has no convention trap. `unmatched_statement_constants` is what the list has no rule for; the list's own not_covered section names the known gaps.

definitions_reviewed.limit: Lean's own definitions are excluded: a reviewer is not expected to have read Init. A statement with none of its own definitions rests entirely on Lean's, which is informative rather than missing -- and note that `AmpasRef.Defs` is NOT excluded even though the provenance layer trusts it, because a wrong `Ampas.IsEven` is the canonical fidelity failure and it lives there.
